title: Scholastics split dulia: hyperdulia for Mary as Lady and Queen, proper dulia for the other Saints
source_text: III. Caeterum quoniam Beata Virgo, ut Mater filii Dei, ita praestat aliis Sanctis ut juxta doctorum illorum sententiam, dici possit Domina & Regina nostra, quod aliis Sanctis non convenit, nisi admodum imperfecte; ideo Scholastici hanc tertiam speciem, quam vocant Duliam, dividunt in Duliam proprie dictam, & Hyperduliam, hanc tribuentes Beatae Virgini, illam vero caeteris Sanctis.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover, since the Blessed Virgin, as Mother of the Son of God, so excels the other Saints that according to the sentence of those doctors she can be called our Lady and Queen, which does not befit the other Saints except very imperfectly; therefore the Scholastics divide this third species, which they call Dulia, into Dulia properly so called, and Hyperdulia, assigning this latter to the Blessed Virgin, but the former to the remaining Saints.
pass_b_english: Mary’s maternity of the Son of God lifts her above other Saints as Lady and Queen.
Hence Schoolmen bisect dulia: hyperdulia for her, proper dulia for the rest.

choices.why: Roman school title for Mary in this locus.
